This notebook documents the shared Linear Mixed-effects Model (LMM) workflow used throughout this repository. Each analysis notebook focuses on dataset-specific preprocessing, visualization, and interpretation, while calling shared functions to perform the statistical analysis.

The shared functions used throughout the repository and defined in `R/LMM_functions.R` are:

-   `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`
-   `format_stats_results()`

## `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`

This function fits a linear mixed-effects model and returns a structured list containing model summaries, ANOVA results, estimated marginal means, and post hoc contrasts.

### Inputs

-   `input_data`: data frame containing the variables used in the model
-   `response`: name of the response variable as a character string
-   `log_response`: logical; if `TRUE`, the response is modeled as `log(response)`
-   `fixed_effects`: character vector of fixed-effect variable names; if more than one fixed effect is provided, interaction terms are included in the model
-   `random_effects1`: first random effect, typically a grouping factor such as `line`
-   `random_effects2`: optional second random effect, typically `date`, used to define an additional random grouping term (`random_effects1:random_effects2`) and as a fallback random effect if singularity is detected
-   `adjust`: p-value adjustment method passed to `emmeans` for multiple comparisons (for example `"holm"`, `"bonferroni"`, or `"fdr"`)

### What it does

The function programmatically constructs a model formula from the supplied arguments. If `log_response = TRUE`, the response variable is log-transformed before fitting. For example:

-   one fixed effect: `log(response) ~ factor1 + (1|line)`
-   two fixed effects: `log(response) ~ factor1 * factor2 + (1|line) + (1|line:date)`

The function then:

-   fits the model with `lmer()` from the **lme4** [@lme4] package
-   checks model singularity with `isSingular()`
-   if singularity is detected and `random_effects2` is provided, simplifies the random-effects structure and refits the model using the same fixed-effects formula but with `(1|random_effects2)` as the random effect
-   extracts summaries of the random and fixed effects
-   computes ANOVA statistics using the **lmerTest** [@lmerTest] package, which provides F-tests and p-values using the default Satterthwaite approximation for denominator degrees of freedom
-   computes estimated marginal means and pairwise contrasts for the specified fixed effects and, when applicable, interaction contrasts, using the **emmeans** [@emmeans] package with p-values adjusted by the specified method
-   returns estimated marginal mean predictions and approximate confidence bounds; if the response variable was log-transformed, these predictions are back-transformed to the original response scale for interpretability

### Outputs

The returned object is a list containing:

-   `input_data`: the input data with a combined `condition` column added for downstream matching and plotting
-   `model_formula`: the fitted model formula
-   `anova`: ANOVA table for the fitted model
-   `random_effects`: variance components extracted from the random-effects structure
-   `fixed_effects`: fixed-effect coefficient table from `summary(model)`
-   `emmeans_formula`: formula used to generate estimated marginal means
-   `emmeans_contrasts`: pairwise contrasts for main effects and, when applicable, interactions
-   `emmeans_predictions`: estimated marginal means with back-transformed predictions and confidence bounds

### Function definition


```r
function (input_data, response, log_response, fixed_effects, 
    random_effects1 = NULL, random_effects2 = NULL, adjust) 
{
    fixed_formula <- paste(fixed_effects, collapse = " * ")
    rand1 <- if (!is.null(random_effects1)) 
        paste0("(1|", random_effects1, ")")
    else NULL
    rand2 <- if (!is.null(random_effects2)) 
        paste0("(1|", random_effects1, ":", random_effects2, 
            ")")
    else NULL
    random_formula <- paste(na.omit(c(rand1, rand2)), collapse = " + ")
    response_part <- if (log_response) {
        paste0("log(", response, ")")
    }
    else {
        response
    }
    formula_str <- paste(response_part, "~", fixed_formula, "+", 
        random_formula)
    model_formula <- as.formula(formula_str)
    model <- lmer(model_formula, data = input_data)
    singular <- isSingular(model)
    random_effects_df <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(model)) %>% mutate(proportion = round(100 * 
        (vcov/sum(vcov)), 2)) %>% mutate(singular = singular)
    if (singular && !is.null(random_effects2)) {
        fallback_formula_str <- paste(response_part, "~", fixed_formula, 
            "+", paste0("(1|", random_effects2, ")"))
        model_formula <- as.formula(fallback_formula_str)
        model <- lmer(model_formula, data = input_data)
    }
    anova_tbl <- anova(model)
    effect_names <- rownames(anova_tbl)
    fixed_effects_df <- as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients) %>% 
        rownames_to_column(var = "term")
    emmeans_formula <- as.formula(paste("~", fixed_formula))
    emmeans_model <- emmeans(model, emmeans_formula)
    emmeans_contrasts <- lapply(fixed_effects, function(effect) {
        summary(pairs(emmeans_model, simple = effect, adjust = adjust))
    })
    names(emmeans_contrasts) <- fixed_effects
    if (length(fixed_effects) > 1) {
        emmeans_contrasts[["interaction"]] <- summary(contrast(emmeans_model, 
            interaction = rep("pairwise", length(fixed_effects)), 
            by = NULL), adjust = adjust)
    }
    emmeans_df <- as.data.frame(emmeans_model)
    emmeans_df <- emmeans_df %>% mutate(predicted_mean = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean)
    else emmean, predicted_lower = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean - 2 * SE)
    else emmean - 2 * SE, predicted_upper = if (log_response) 
        exp(emmean + 2 * SE)
    else emmean + 2 * SE, condition = paste(!!!syms(fixed_effects), 
        sep = ".")) %>% filter(!is.na(emmean)) %>% droplevels()
    input_data <- input_data %>% mutate(condition = paste(!!!syms(fixed_effects), 
        sep = "."))
    return(list(input_data = input_data, model_formula = model_formula, 
        anova = anova_tbl, random_effects = random_effects_df, 
        fixed_effects = fixed_effects_df, emmeans_formula = emmeans_formula, 
        emmeans_contrasts = emmeans_contrasts, emmeans_predictions = emmeans_df))
}
```


## `format_stats_results()`

This function takes the output of `mixed_model_with_emmeans()` and reformats it into tidy tables that are easier to join, filter, annotate, and plot.

### Inputs

-   `stats_results`: the list returned by `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`
-   `grouping_vars`: variables used to summarize the original observed data alongside model predictions. The default is `condition`, a combined variable created in `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`, but additional variables from the original data can be included when needed for downstream plotting or annotation.
-   `p.value_threshold`: threshold used to create a simple significance label column (`sign`); the default is `0.05`

### What it does

This function:

-   summarizes the original observed data by group and calculates the mean and standard error for each group, which can be used for plotting alongside model predictions
-   joins those summaries to the `emmeans` predictions
-   matches each contrast to its corresponding predicted means, allowing calculation of fold changes (FC) and log2 fold changes (log2FC) between contrast groups
-   returns a clean structure for downstream visualization and reporting, including columns named `group1` and `group2` that can be used to annotate significant differences in plots, as well as a simple significance label (`sign`) based on the specified p-value threshold

### Outputs

The returned object is a list containing:

-   `input_data`: the original input data with a combined `condition` column
-   `predictions`: estimated marginal means joined with observed summary statistics
-   `main`: formatted main-effect contrasts with columns for `group1`, `group2`, `FC`, `log2FC`, and `sign`
-   `interaction`: formatted interaction contrasts, if present
-   `anova`: passed through from `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`
-   `random_effects`: passed through from `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`
-   `fixed_effects`: passed through from `mixed_model_with_emmeans()`

### Function definition


```r
function (stats_results, grouping_vars = c("condition"), p.value_threshold = 0.05) 
{
    input_data <- stats_results$input_data
    predictions <- stats_results$emmeans_predictions
    contrasts <- stats_results$emmeans_contrasts
    response <- stats_results$model_formula[[2]]
    anova <- stats_results$anova
    random_effects <- stats_results$random_effects
    fixed_effects <- stats_results$fixed_effects
    if (is.call(response) && identical(response[[1]], as.name("log"))) {
        response <- response[[2]]
    }
    input_summary <- input_data %>% group_by(across(all_of(grouping_vars))) %>% 
        summarise(n = n(), mean = mean({
            {
                response
            }
        }), sd = sd({
            {
                response
            }
        }), se = sd/sqrt(n), .groups = "drop")
    predictions <- predictions %>% left_join(input_summary, by = "condition")
    effect_names <- names(contrasts)
    main_effects <- setdiff(effect_names, "interaction")
    has_interaction <- "interaction" %in% effect_names
    anova_effect_names <- rownames(stats_results$anova)
    anova_pvalues <- stats_results$anova$`Pr(>F)`
    names(anova_pvalues) <- anova_effect_names
    process_main_effect <- function(name) {
        contr <- contrasts[[name]]
        contr$effect_name <- name
        contr$p.value.anova <- anova_pvalues[name]
        contr <- contr %>% mutate(contrast = str_replace_all(contrast, 
            "\\s+", ""))
        contr <- contr %>% separate(contrast, into = c("condition1", 
            "condition2"), sep = "-", remove = FALSE, fill = "right")
        other_effect <- setdiff(main_effects, name)
        if (length(other_effect) == 1 && other_effect %in% names(contr)) {
            if (name == main_effects[1]) {
                contr <- contr %>% mutate(condition1 = paste(condition1, 
                  .data[[other_effect]], sep = "."), condition2 = paste(condition2, 
                  .data[[other_effect]], sep = "."))
            }
            else {
                contr <- contr %>% mutate(condition1 = paste(.data[[other_effect]], 
                  condition1, sep = "."), condition2 = paste(.data[[other_effect]], 
                  condition2, sep = "."))
            }
        }
        contr
    }
    main_contrasts <- lapply(main_effects, process_main_effect)
    main_contrasts_tbl <- bind_rows(main_contrasts) %>% select(effect_name, 
        p.value.anova, contrast, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, 
        everything())
    main_contrasts_tbl <- main_contrasts_tbl %>% left_join(dplyr::select(predictions, 
        condition, predicted_mean), by = join_by(condition1 == 
        condition)) %>% left_join(dplyr::select(predictions, 
        condition, predicted_mean), by = join_by(condition2 == 
        condition), suffix = c(".1", ".2")) %>% mutate(FC = predicted_mean.1/predicted_mean.2, 
        log2FC = log2(FC), sign = case_when(p.value < p.value_threshold ~ 
            "*", TRUE ~ ""))
    conditions_label_col = grouping_vars[1]
    main_contrasts_tbl$group1 <- predictions[[conditions_label_col]][match(main_contrasts_tbl$condition1, 
        predictions$condition)]
    main_contrasts_tbl$group2 <- predictions[[conditions_label_col]][match(main_contrasts_tbl$condition2, 
        predictions$condition)]
    interaction_tbl <- NULL
    if (has_interaction) {
        inter_contr <- contrasts$interaction
        inter_contr$effect_name <- "interaction"
        interaction_anova_name <- names(anova_pvalues)[grepl(":", 
            names(anova_pvalues))]
        inter_contr$p.value.anova <- anova_pvalues[interaction_anova_name]
        interaction_tbl <- inter_contr %>% select(effect_name, 
            p.value.anova, estimate, SE, df, t.ratio, p.value, 
            everything()) %>% mutate(sign = case_when(p.value < 
            p.value_threshold ~ "*", TRUE ~ ""))
    }
    return(list(input_data = input_data, predictions = predictions, 
        main = main_contrasts_tbl, interaction = interaction_tbl, 
        anova = anova, random_effects = random_effects, fixed_effects = fixed_effects))
}
```
